questions.question: 20 women and 15 men together can complete a work in 6 days. One woman takes 150 days to complete the work. In how many days can one man complete the same work? 20
questions.solution:
Step 1   What 20 women do in a day. 
20 × 1/150 = 2/15 
 Step 2   So the 15 men supply the rest of the 1/6. 
1/6 − 2/15 = 1/30   ⇒  one man = 1/450   ∴  450 
days

questions.question: A, B and C together can complete a work in 12 days. A and B respectively alone can complete the same work in 36 and 36 days. In how many days can C alone complete the same work? A, B
questions.solution:
Step 1   A and B together. 
1/36 + 1/36 = 1/18 
 Step 2   C is the difference. 
1/12 − 1/18 = 1/36   ∴  C alone takes 36 days

questions.question: A can complete a work in 8 days by working 5 hours per day and B can complete the same work in 10 days by working 6 hours per day. If both worked together for 8 hours a day, how many days will they take to complete the work? A Ů
questions.solution:
Step 1   Total hours each needs. 
A : 8 × 5 = 40 h        B : 10 × 6 = 60 h 
 Step 2   Take the job as 120 units. 
A = 3/h,  B = 2/h   ⇒  together 5/h   ⇒  120/5 = 24 
hours 
 Step 3   At 8 hours a day. 
24 / 8 = 3 days

questions.question: S₁ and S₂ together can do a piece of work in 18 days, S₂ and S₃ together in 27 days, while S₃ and S₁ together can do it in 54 days. In how many days can all three working together do 50% of work? S₁
questions.solution:
Step 1   Add. 
1/18 + 1/27 + 1/54 = 6/54 = 1/9 = 2(S₁ + S₂ + S₃) 
 Step 2   So all three together. 
rate = 1/18   ⇒  the whole job in 18 days 
 Step 3   The question wants half the job. 
18 / 2 = 9 days

questions.question: A and B together can complete a work in 48 days. A is four times as efficient as B. In how many days can B alone complete the work? A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write both rates in B's units. 
A = 4B   ⇒  A + B = 5B = 1/48 
 Step 2   So B alone. 
B = 1/240   ∴  240 days

questions.question: A can do ¼th of the work in 9 days. B can do ²⁄3of the same work in 28 days. In how many days will A and B complete the same work while working together? A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Full-job times. 
A : ¼ in 9 days  ⇒  36 days        B : ⅔ in 28 days  
⇒  42 days 
 Step 2   Add the rates. 
1/36 + 1/42 = 13/252   ⇒  252/13 days

questions.question: A can complete a work in 16 days and B can complete the same work in 12 days. They worked together for 4 days and then A left, then B completed the remaining work alone. For how many days did B work to complete the work? A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Take the job as 48 units. 
A = 3/day,  B = 4/day 
 Step 2   Four days together. 
(3 + 4) × 4 = 28 units   ⇒  20 left 
 Step 3   B finishes alone. 
20 / 4 = 5 days   ∴  B worked 4 + 5 = 9 days in 
all

questions.question: A and B do a piece of work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. They worked together for 4 days after which B was replaced by C and remaining work was completed by A and C in next 4 days. In how many days will C alone complete 50% of the same work? A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Take the job as 36 units. 
A = 3/day,  B = 2/day   ⇒  4 days together = 20 
units,  16 left 
 Step 2   A and C clear those 16 in 4 days. 
A + C = 4/day   ⇒  C = 1/day 
 Step 3   So C alone, for half the job. 
36 / 1 = 36 days   ⇒  50% = 18 days

questions.question: A does half as much as B in ¹⁄₆th time. If together they take 16 days to complete the work, how many days will B alone take to complete the work? A, B
questions.solution:
Step 1   Turn it into rates. 
A's rate = (1/2) ÷ (1/6) = 3 times B's   ⇒  A = 3B 
 Step 2   Together they are 4B. 
4B = 1/16   ⇒  B = 1/64   ∴  64 days

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 20 days while B can do the same work in 25 days. Both of them work together for 10 days and C alone completes the remaining work in 10 days. In how many days will A, B and C together complete the same work? A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Take the job as 100 units. 
A = 5/day,  B = 4/day   ⇒  10 days together = 90 
units,  10 left 
 Step 2   C clears 10 units in 10 days. 
C = 1/day 
 Step 3   All three. 
100 / (5 + 4 + 1) = 10 days

questions.question: B would have taken 10 hours more than what A would have taken to complete a task if each worked alone. Working together they can complete the task in 12 hours. How many hours would B take to do 50% of the task? B
questions.solution:
Step 1   Add the rates. 
1/a + 1/(a + 10) = 1/12 
 Step 2   Clear and factorise. 
a² − 14a − 120 = 0   ⇒  (a − 20)(a + 6) = 0   ⇒  a = 
20,  B = 30 
 Step 3   Half the task for B. 
30 / 2 = 15 hours

questions.question: A can do 40% of a work in 12 days, whereas B can do 60% of the same work in 15 days. Both work together for 10 days. C completes the remaining work alone in 4 days. A, B and C together will complete 28% of the same work in: A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Full-job times, and the job as 150 units. 
A : 40% in 12 days ⇒ 30 days ⇒ 5/day        B : 
60% in 15 days ⇒ 25 days ⇒ 6/day 
 Step 2   Ten days together, then C. 
11 × 10 = 110 units   ⇒  40 left,  cleared by C in 4 
days   ⇒  C = 10/day 
 Step 3   All three on 28% of the job. 
28% of 150 = 42   ⇒  42 / 21 = 2 days

questions.question: A and B together can do certain work in x days. Working alone, A and B can do the same work in (x+8) and (x+18) days respectively. A and B together will complete 5/6 of the same work in: A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Add the two individual rates to the joint 
one. 
1/(x + 8) + 1/(x + 18) = 1/x 
 Step 2   Clear. 
x(2x + 26) = (x + 8)(x + 18)   ⇒  x² = 144   ⇒  x = 12 
 Step 3   Five-sixths of the job. 
12 × 5/6 = 10 days

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B and C is thrice as efficient as B. Working together, they can finish a certain work in 5 days. A and C worked together for 5 days. B alone would complete the remaining work in ______. A, B
questions.solution:
Step 1   A = 2B and C = 3B. 
A + B + C = 6B = 1/5   ⇒  B = 1/30 
 Step 2   A and C for five days. 
(5B) × 5 = 25/30 = 5/6 done   ⇒  1/6 left 
 Step 3   B finishes it. 
(1/6) ÷ (1/30) = 5 days

questions.question: A can do one-third of a job in 15 days. B can do 75% of the same job in 18 days and C can do the same job in 36 days. B and C work together for 8 days. In how many days will A alone complete the remaining work? A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Full-job times, and the job as 360 units. 
A : ⅓ in 15 ⇒ 45 days ⇒ 8/day        B : 75% in 18 
⇒ 24 days ⇒ 15/day        C : 36 days ⇒ 10/day 
 Step 2   B and C for eight days. 
25 × 8 = 200 units   ⇒  160 left 
 Step 3   A alone. 
160 / 8 = 20 days

units,  10 left

questions.question: P can complete five-eighths of a work in 15 days and Q can complete three-fourths of the same work in 30 days. They worked together for 8 days and then P left. How much time will Q working alone take to complete the remaining work? P
questions.solution:
Step 1   Full-job times, job as 120 units. 
P : ⅝ in 15 ⇒ 24 days ⇒ 5/day        Q : ¾ in 30 ⇒ 
40 days ⇒ 3/day 
 Step 2   Eight days together. 
8 × 8 = 64 units   ⇒  56 left 
 Step 3   Q alone. 
56 / 3 = 18⅔ days = 18 days 16 hours

questions.question: The ratio of the efficiencies of A, B and C is 7:5:4. Working together, they can finish a work in 35 days. A and B work together for 28 days. The remaining work will be completed (in days) by C alone: A, B
questions.solution:
Step 1   7 + 5 + 4 = 16 units a day for 35 days. 
job = 16 × 35 = 560 units 
 Step 2   A and B for 28 days. 
12 × 28 = 336   ⇒  224 left 
 Step 3   C alone at 4 a day. 
224 / 4 = 56 days

questions.question: To do a certain work, the ratio of the efficiencies of A, B and C is 7:5:6. Working together, they complete the work in 35 days. B and C work together for 21 days. The remaining work will be completed by A alone in:
questions.solution:
Step 1   7 + 5 + 6 = 18 a day for 35 days. 
job = 630 units 
 Step 2   B and C for 21 days. 
11 × 21 = 231   ⇒  399 left 
 Step 3   A alone at 7 a day. 
399 / 7 = 57 days

questions.question: A group of men decided to do a work in 6 days but every day 18 men left the job. If the work is completed in 8 days, how many men initially decided to do that work?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Planned against actual. 
planned = 6m        actual = m + (m − 18) + … + 
(m − 126) = 8m − 18(0+1+…+7) 
 Step 2   Equate them. 
8m − 504 = 6m   ⇒  2m = 504   ∴  m = 252 men

questions.question: Four men and 6 women can complete a certain piece of work in 5 days whereas three men and 4 women can complete it in 7 days. How many men should assist 25 women to complete 2½ times the same work in 5 days?
questions.solution:
Step 1   Write both. 
4M + 6W = 1/5        3M + 4W = 1/7 
 Step 2   Eliminate M. 
2W = 3/5 − 4/7 = 1/35   ⇒  W = 1/70,  and then M 
= 1/35 
 Step 3   The requirement: 2½ jobs in 5 days. 
rate needed = 1/2   ⇒  x/35 + 25/70 = 1/2   ⇒  x/35 
= 1/7   ∴  x = 5 men

questions.solution:
Step 1   Let A take a days. 
B = 5.4a,  and 5.4a − a = 22   ⇒  4.4a = 22   ⇒  a = 
5,  B = 27 
 Step 2   Together. 
(5 × 27)/(5 + 27) = 135/32 = 4 7/32 days

questions.question: A alone can do ²⁄₅ of a work in 12 days. B is 25% more efficient than A. C alone can do the same work in 12 days less than B. D is 25% less efficient than C. If they all work together, in how many days will the work be completed? A
questions.solution:
Step 1   A, then B, then C, then D. 
A : ⅖ in 12 days ⇒ 30 days        B : 25% faster ⇒ 
30/1.25 = 24 days 
C : 12 days less than B ⇒ 12 days        D : 25% 
slower than C ⇒ 12/0.75 = 16 days 
 Step 2   Add the rates over 240. 
8 + 10 + 20 + 15 = 53/240 
 Step 3   Invert. 
240/53 days

questions.question: A and B working separately can do a piece of work in 21 and 24 days, respectively. If they work for a day alternately with A beginning the work, it would be completed in ______. A
questions.solution:
Step 1   Take the job as 168 units. 
A = 8/day,  B = 7/day   ⇒  one cycle = 15 units 
 Step 2   How many whole cycles fit. 
11 cycles = 22 days = 165 units   ⇒  3 left 
 Step 3   Day 23 is A's turn. 
3/8 of a day   ∴  22⅜ days
